parts/room-9.mjs furnishes the flat 1E front room as a sitting room: oriel window seat (3 dark_oak_stairs facing the doorway line) with a fence-and-slab table and two chairs, bookcases (dark_oak_planks with flower pots) on the west and east walls, and 3 hanging lanterns under the y 18 ceiling.</summary>
<parameter name="finished">true
left: No rug: carpet is not in palette.json, and a wool block at y 14 would be a solid obstacle on the walk, so the rug is left out.

The walk verdict is OK, but mcd room lists 4 'unreached' cells: the bookcase tops at y 16 (pots' neighbours standing on top of the planks). They are not floor cells, so I did not fix them; the tool counts them as floor.
Light min 8, mean 10.1, 0 dark, 0 dim: the 'Light: all rooms >= 8' item in elements.md is a whole-building item, so I did not tick it.
Bookshelves read as planks with pots, not as books: no bookshelf or barrel is in palette.json.
make.sh ran clean; my part placed 27 blocks with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines. The check's 8 orphans and enclosed cells are in other parts, not in this room.

waste.what: Worked out the layer rows by hand (x mod 10 columns, z row order) and checked each pot and planks cell by reading the built NBT through a node one-liner, because the room tool's unreached list named cells I could not place from the output.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls and one node one-off to confirm the pots at (13,16,13), (20,16,14), (20,16,16).
waste.tool: mcd room should print each unreached cell with its block and the block under it, and say when it is a bookcase top, not a floor cell.

waste.what: Chose lantern spots by eye, then measured the light map once. The room came out at min 8, which was luck, not design.
waste.cost: one make.sh, one room check, no retries.
waste.tool: mcd room --suggest-lanterns should place lanterns that clear the dark cells, so the hand choice is checked by the tool before the build.

waste.what: Drew the furniture as a text grid and mapped it onto each y layer by hand: 4 layers, 7 rows each.
